cands.name: Michael Owen
cands.bio: Civil-litigation / real-estate attorney (Owen & Dunivan PLLC). Born 1975 in Houston, raised in Brandon, FL; Saint Leo University B.A. Hillsborough County Commissioner (District 4, vice chair 2023-24) and Port Tampa Bay board member from Dec 2022; resigned from commission June 2024 to run for the House. Elected Nov 2024.
cands.local_ties: Raised in Brandon (Hillsborough County); district office listed in Apollo Beach. District is roughly 70 percent Hillsborough and 30 percent Manatee per Osprey Observer. His Manatee portion includes the northern edge of the 34221 area; he is primarily a Hillsborough figure and his current residence was not stated in sources found.

record.text: Voted Yea on SB 180 (2025 post-hurricane preemption of local planning rules): House passage 4/29/2025 (115-1) and concurrence 5/2/2025 (106-0).
Voted Yea on HB 399 (2026 Land Use and Development Regulations), both House passage 3/3/2026 (71-38) and final concurrence 3/13/2026 (73-27); signed 3/27/2026 as Chapter 2026-7.
Voted Yea on CS/HJR 1-F (June 2, 2026) placing the homestead property-tax exemption increase on the Nov 2026 ballot (House 75-26).

Sponsored HB 4027 (2026): Hillsborough referendum making the school superintendent elected (House 86-26, Senate 36-0; Ch. 2026-196). The companion Hillsborough commission-expansion referendum is also on the Nov 2026 ballot.

2025 sponsored bills include HB 1517 (civil liability for wrongful death of an unborn child) and HB 1489 (kratom products); filed a constitutional term-limits proposal in Feb 2025 (2 four-year Senate terms, 4 two-year House terms). 2026 bills HB 705 (causes of action based on improvements to real property) and HB 489 (Florida Housing Finance Corp terminology) are listed as failed.
As a county commissioner he announced a plan to dissolve HART and establish a Tampa-only transit system.
Did not serve in the Legislature in 2023, so no vote on SB 264 (foreign land ownership).

foreign_ties.text: None documented in the public records searched (FARA filings, foreign-government payments, state-owned business, foreign-agent donors).

endorsements.text: Multiple Tampa Bay area sheriffs endorsed Owen in 2024 as a 'champion for public safety' (Florida Politics; article paywalled, names not retrieved).

local_issue_stance.text: Candidate questionnaire: calls Florida's greatest challenge 'managing our continued growth while preserving the affordability, freedoms, and quality of life'; lists infrastructure and natural resources among priorities but gives no specifics on wetlands or home rule.
Voted Yea on SB 180 and HB 399 (both limit local land-use authority).

cands.name: Luther Keith Wilkins
cands.bio: U.S. Army sergeant 1984-96; sales manager; publisher of the Manatee County Black Chamber of Commerce (since 2019); president of the Manatee County NAACP (since 2022); insurance producer at Globe Life (2026-); logistics specialist at Smurfit Westrock 2020-25. Ran against Owen in 2024 as well and lost.
cands.local_ties: Manatee County civic leader (NAACP president, Black Chamber publisher); exact residence not found.

record.text: No legislative record (never elected). Platform: affordable housing and 'responsible growth', veterans' services (VA healthcare, transportation), higher teacher pay, infrastructure, water quality and wetland restoration.
Chamber questionnaire: supports strengthening land-use rules, protecting habitats, stormwater upgrades, stricter industrial/agricultural discharge rules.

money_notes.text: In 2024 coverage, Florida Politics noted Wilkins retained only about $430 in his account (versus Owen's law-enforcement backing and fundraising). No 2026 figures found.
